results.content: In 2025, the Trump Administration imposed a 25% global tariff on U.S. imports of certain automotive product s, including vehicles, under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962. Goods that meet USMCA automotive ROO are largely, but not wholly, exempt from these tariffs. Data suggest that in 2025 around 84% of U.S. auto imports from Canada and Mexico met USMCA content rules but were subject to certain tariff actions. results.content:
The 15% rate for Japanese imports will not "stack" on top of existing tariff rates—i.e., it is inclusive of any most-favored nation (MFN) tariff rate above zero applied to goods not traded under a free trade agreement. If the MFN rate is above 15%, no IEEPA tariff is applied to Japanese goods.
   Japanese automotive products face a 15% tariff, inclusive of MFN rates. Section 232 tariffs on Japanese steel, aluminum, and copper remain at 50%.
